name: Tin-glazed earthenware painted in lustre (William De Morgan's lustreware)

diffuseAlbedo.note: The white a photograph of the ware's white stands for: the tin glaze's warm white; no measured colour was read.

refractiveIndex.source: Shading/Substances/glaze.celadon.json (a ceramic glaze is a soda-lime-alumina-silica glass of about 1.52)

porosity.source: a fired tin glaze is a glass fused to the body (the reasoning the frit.white and opal-glass records already use)
porosity.note: The value is unchanged, and the grade follows the reasoning the frit and opal records already accept. Any bubbles in a glaze are closed, so they add no open porosity. Caveat: tin glaze on earthenware often crazes, and crazed ware lets water reach the porous body. That belongs to a history, not to this sound-glaze value.
porosity.derivation: a fused glass layer has no open pores

wettingDepth.derivation: with no pores, nothing wets its body
